title: Proverbs 19
paragraphs: ¹ Better to be poor and walk in integrity than to be perverse in speech and be a fool. ² Desire without knowledge is not good — and how much more will hasty feet miss the way! ³ A person's own foolishness leads them astray, yet their heart rages against the LORD. ⁴ Wealth attracts many friends, but the poor are deserted by their friends. ⁵ A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will not go free.

⁶ Many curry favor with a ruler, and everyone is the friend of those who give gifts. ⁷ The poor are shunned by all their relatives — how much more do their friends avoid them! They pursue them with pleading, but find nothing. ⁸ Whoever gets wisdom loves life; whoever cherishes understanding will prosper. ⁹ A false witness will not go unpunished, and whoever pours out lies will perish. ¹⁰ It is not fitting for a fool to live in luxury — how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!

¹¹ A person's wisdom gives them patience; it is to their glory to overlook an offense. ¹² A king's rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass. ¹³ A foolish child is a father's ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping. ¹⁴ Houses and wealth are inherited from parents, but a prudent wife comes from the LORD. ¹⁵ Laziness plunges a person into deep sleep, and the idle go hungry.

¹⁶ Whoever keeps the commandment keeps their life, but whoever despises their ways will die. ¹⁷ Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and he will repay them for what they have done. ¹⁸ Discipline your children, for in that there is hope; do not be a willing party to their death. ¹⁹ A hot-tempered person must pay the penalty; rescue them, and you will have to do it again. ²⁰ Listen to counsel and accept instruction, so that you may be wise for the rest of your days.

²¹ Many are the plans in a person's heart, but it is the LORD's purpose that prevails. ²² What a person desires is kindness; it is better to be poor than to be a liar. ²³ The fear of the LORD leads to life; a person rests content, untouched by trouble. ²⁴ A lazy person puts their hand in the dish and won't even lift it back to their mouth. ²⁵ Strike a mocker and the simple will learn wisdom; correct the discerning and they gain knowledge.

²⁶ Whoever robs their father and drives out their mother is a child who brings shame and disgrace. ²⁷ Stop listening, my son, to teaching that leads you away from the words of knowledge. ²⁸ A corrupt witness mocks justice, and the mouth of the wicked swallows up iniquity. ²⁹ Penalties are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
